package_info.why_malicious: The Ring Android app contained an exported activity that allowed untrusted apps to load attacker-controlled web content into a privileged WebView, enabling theft of sensitive authorization tokens and subsequent exfiltration of personal and device data.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, a malicious app sends an intent to the exported DeepLinkActivity with a crafted URL, causing the Ring app to load attacker-controlled web content in a privileged WebView.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exported activities should not accept arbitrary external input, especially URLs, without validation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps restrict exported activities and validate input; here, the activity is open and loads untrusted content.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Deep linking to trusted, internal app content.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malicious web page exploits a reflected XSS vulnerability to inject JavaScript, which calls the privileged __NATIVE_BRIDGE__.getToken() interface, exfiltrating the Ring authorization token to an attacker-controlled server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: WebView JavaScript interfaces should not be exposed to untrusted content; exfiltration of tokens is a classic sign of credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal WebViews restrict JavaScript interfaces to trusted origins; here, attacker-controlled content can access sensitive APIs.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Trusted in-app web content using JavaScript bridges for legitimate features.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After exfiltrating the token and hardware ID, the attacker obtains a session cookie and uses Ring APIs to extract personal data, device geolocation, and camera recordings.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated use of stolen credentials to access sensitive APIs is a hallmark of account/data compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: APIs are intended for authenticated user devices, not remote attackers using stolen tokens.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate app/server access by authenticated users.
key_indicators: Use of session cookies from unauthorized context

attack_chain.action: Malicious app sends intent to exported DeepLinkActivity with attacker-controlled URL.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ring app loads attacker-controlled web content in privileged WebView.

attack_chain.action: Attacker web page exploits XSS to inject JavaScript, accesses __NATIVE_BRIDGE__.getToken(), and exfiltrates token.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker obtains Ring authorization token and hardware ID.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses token and hardware ID to obtain session cookie and access Ring APIs for personal and device data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of personal data, geolocation, and camera recordings.

behavioral_signatures: Exported Android activities accepting arbitrary external URLs
WebView loading untrusted content with JavaScript interfaces enabled
Unusual API calls from non-standard device fingerprints
Bulk access to user/device data shortly after app-to-app intent
file_indicators: WebView components with addJavascriptInterface enabled for sensitive APIs
network_indicators: Outbound requests to attacker-controlled domains (e.g., MALICIOUS.DOMAIN.COM)
Unusual access to https://ring.com/mobile/authorize and related APIs from new device fingerprints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for exported activities that accept external URLs, WebViews with JavaScript interfaces exposed to untrusted origins, and anomalous API usage patterns (e.g., session cookie requests and bulk data access) following inter-app intents. Flag outbound network requests to suspicious domains and look for reflected XSS payloads in trusted subdomains.
